name: HUMPIRE CLUTCH
tagline: Compressor with Clean, Punch and Crush modes, sidechain high-pass, parallel mix and a LED life bar.
sub: Clean, Punch and Crush with parallel mix
gumroad_title: HUMPIRE CLUTCH - Compressor VST3 + AU Plugin (12 Presets) | Clean, Punch, Crush
summary: A compressor plugin with three modes (Clean, Punch and Crush), soft knee, sidechain high-pass filter and a parallel mix control.
about: HUMPIRE CLUTCH is a feed-forward compressor with a soft knee and a gain-reduction display drawn as a 32-segment life bar that drains as you compress, with a history graph below it.
Clean is a transparent compressor. Punch slows the attack and shortens the release so the transient passes through. Crush multiplies the ratio, speeds up the attack and adds saturation.
A one-pole sidechain high-pass (20 to 500 Hz) keeps low frequencies from triggering the compressor, and the Mix control blends the dry and compressed signals for parallel compression.

features.d: Clean, Punch (lets the attack through) and Crush (higher ratio, faster attack, saturation).
Threshold -40 to 0 dB, ratio 1:1 to 20:1, attack 0.1 to 100 ms, release 10 to 1000 ms, knee 0 to 24 dB.
20 to 500 Hz, so bass does not over-trigger the detector.
Blend dry and compressed signals from 0 to 100%.
A 32-segment bar and a history graph show the gain reduction up to 24 dB.
Factory presets grouped by category, user presets saved by name, A/B compare, undo and redo.
Scales from 50% to 200% with the proportions locked. Simple and Clean display modes.

includes: HUMPIRE CLUTCH plugin (Windows VST3; macOS VST3 + Audio Unit)

faq.q: Which DAWs does it work in?
faq.a: It is a VST3 effect on Windows and macOS, plus Audio Unit on macOS. It is designed for FL Studio and should load in any host that supports these formats.

faq.q: What is the difference between the three modes?
faq.a: Clean compresses as set. Punch lengthens the attack and shortens the release to keep the transient. Crush raises the ratio, shortens the attack and adds saturation.

faq.q: Can I save my own presets?
faq.a: Yes. The SAVE button stores the current settings under a name you choose, and they appear in the User category of the preset menu.
